messages:
incident-bot: Pager: KV cache continuous-batching error rate > 5% on prod (region: us-west-2). Auto-escalation to oncall. Incident ID INC-2794440000 :rotating_light:

alice_oncall: seeing big p50->p95 latency spike and 502s in the gateway dashboards. Is this the same continuous-batching regression from last month?

bob_sre: yep, looks like a runaway KV cache growth — eviction thrash + long tail batches. Memory pressure on some shards, OOM-protect kicking in. Node group `kvc-uw2-05` showing repeated restarts.

carol_runtime: stack traces show huge KV cache maps for some prefixes. Dump snippet: ```
KVShard(id=42) size=1.2M entries; top prefixes: \"/user/stream/\" (420k), \"/sys/prefix-blob\" (380k)```

alice_oncall: which models are the requests hitting?

carol_runtime: mix of Llama-2-70B (mq-quant), Mistral-7B-v2 (gqa), and Qwen-14B-MQA. Qwen shards show heavy multi-query aggregation — batch sizes spiking to 4x expected.

dave_ml: that combination rings alarm bells. Qwen's MQA client merges requests differently; when prefix cardinality is high, continuous batching can accumulate many distinct KV contexts. Mistral gqa path also keeps larger KV states per prompt.

erica_support: we have 5 customers with active requests hitting those models right now; 2 reported timeouts (support ticket: #34221, #34222). I left a quick reply to let them know we're investigating.

frank_cs: customer A (payments) is seeing multi-second tail latency on embeddings endpoints. They want ETA.

alice_oncall: immediate mitigations: 1) throttling ingress to affected shards, 2) disable continuous-batching config for Qwen/GQA Mistral paths, 3) increase cache eviction aggressiveness. Can someone run the config toggles?

hector_eng: I can flip the gating flag for continuous batching to "disabled" for model routes `qwen-*` and `mistral-*` in the runtime config. Will do a canary on one shard first.

carol_runtime: deploying toggle via `runtime-config set --path /batching/continuous/enabled false --selector shard=qwen-uw2-05` now. Canary applying to shard-42. Logs: ```
[10:18:02] applying config
[10:18:04] canary ok (10 reqs)
```

alice_oncall: good. Meanwhile, reduce max_batch_tokens globally to 1024 from 4096 to avoid oversized batches. That should cut aggregation.

bob_sre: applied token cap on gateway: `gateway.max_batch_tokens=1024` across us-west-2. Watching.

carol_runtime: after canary, shard-42 mem usage dropped ~30% and p95 latency improved. Rolling to remaining Qwen + Mistral shards now.

dave_ml: for Llama-2-70B, we should avoid full disable — it's sensitive to quantization profile; instead reduce KV retention TTL for prefix caches to 10s (was 120s). That will avoid long-lived huge maps for Llama prefixes.

hector_eng: applying KV TTL change for Llama routes: `kvcfg set prefix_ttl 10s --models llama-*` -> rolling update.

erica_support: customer A confirms latency improved after the initial throttle. They still want a postmortem and root cause.

frank_cs: estimated impacted calls: ~13k requests in the window, ~0.7% error rate spike at peak, top customers: PaymentCo, DocuHub.

gina_product: flagging potential SLA breach for PaymentCo. Product wants a mitigation note and workaround (route to dedicated model variant or older quant).

alice_oncall: next steps: 1) finish rollout of disable for Qwen/Mistral continuous batching; 2) apply Llama TTL change; 3) evict the largest prefixes from KV shards to reclaim memory quickly (manual eviction script); 4) inform customers and run retro. Who owns eviction?

carol_runtime: I wrote an eviction script: ```
# evict top prefixes > 100k entries
python tools/kv_eviction.py --shard 42 --min_entries 100000
```
I can run it but will coordinate with SRE to avoid double-evict loops.

bob_sre: run it on the drained nodes first. I'll cordon `kvc-uw2-05` and run eviction on one node, then monitor restart.

hector_eng: eviction complete on node-1. Memory back to normal, restarts stopped. Rolling to node-2.

alice_oncall: monitoring telemetry: p50 stable, p95 trending down, error rate back under threshold. Good.

dave_ml: blocker for root cause: why did the prefixes explode? Early hypothesis: a customer integration started sending highly entropic prefixes (request IDs in the prompt) which increases prefix cardinality and defeats KV prefix compression heuristics. Combined with Qwen MQA merging and continuous batching, it caused combinatorial KV state growth.

frank_cs: confirmed PaymentCo recently deployed a change around 09:50 that altered prompt scaffolding. They've shared sample prompts that include per-request UUIDs at the start.

gina_product: recommend adding best-practice guidance to DevDocs about avoiding high-cardinality prefixes and providing sample templates. Can we get that asap?

irina_devex: I'll draft a short guidance note and a warning to be surfaced in the console for customers hitting large prefix cardinality patterns. Also adding a lint rule to the prompt analyzer.

alice_oncall: customer-facing messaging: frank, erica — send initial update: issue identified as KV growth from high-cardinality prefixes + continuous-batching interaction. Temporary mitigations applied (throttles, batching toggles, TTL reduction, eviction). Full postmortem within 48 hours.

erica_support: sending message to PaymentCo and DocuHub now. Will include ETA and mitigation steps (route to dedicated endpoint if they need zero-latency).

bob_sre: action items for during-incident: 
- track shard restarts and memory usage (SRE)
- finish config rollback toggles once stable (Runtime)
- collect sample prompts and sensor logs (ML / Support)
- notify customers, update status page (CS/Product)

carol_runtime: runtime note: when we re-enable continuous batching we should gate by prefix-cardinality: only enable if unique_prefixes_in_window < 10k. Adding a sensor and safe-fallback to per-request mode.

dave_ml: long-term: add adaptive batching that respects KV cache footprint and per-model profiles (different for MQA vs GQA). Also consider per-customer prefix-normalization utilities.

hector_eng: I'm capturing the remediation commands we ran into the incident runbook: ```
# toggles we used
runtime-config set /batching/continuous/enabled false --selector model=qwen-*
runtime-config set /batching/continuous/enabled false --selector model=mistral-*
kvctl set-prefix-ttl --model llama-* --ttl 10s
gateway set max_batch_tokens=1024
# eviction
python tools/kv_eviction.py --shard 42 --min_entries 100000
```

alice_oncall: team, we're ~45m in. Current status: ingress throttles in place, continuous batching disabled for Qwen/Mistral, Llama TTL reduced, prefix eviction done. Monitoring for regressions. No customers in critical outage; some elevated latencies persisted for 15m window.

frank_cs: PaymentCo says previous 502s vanished after your changes and they are back to normal. They requested a follow-up call tomorrow.

gina_product: ok schedule follow-up and request logs. We'll include a mitigation offer (3 days of dedicated instances free) if SLA breach confirmed.

irina_devex: drafting console warning docs and a sample prefix sanitizer snippet for customers.

bob_sre: setting P1->P2 after stabilization. We'll keep incident open for postmortem.

alice_oncall: preparing handoff to next oncall: @bob_sre will take primary monitoring overnight, @carol_runtime owns rollback plan and re-enable gating once sensors look good. Postmortem owners: @dave_ml (root cause analysis) and @irina_devex (customer guidance + docs).

hector_eng: leaving notes in the runbook channel and marking the runbook update PR.

alice_oncall: final round — anything else?

erica_support: I'll send the outbound update to all affected customers summarizing impact: window, affected models, mitigation, next steps.

gina_product: adding retro meeting invite for 48h and tagging legal for SLA review.

alice_oncall: OK. Closing this slack thread; incident remains open in pager duty (INC-2794440000) until postmortem. Good job team :clap:

incident-bot: Incident marked \"stabilized\" by alice_oncall at 11:20 UTC. Next update expected within 48 hours.
